answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to post a small refundable stake that unlocks only after a long, verifiable history of useful work. Like a glacier moving slowly, reputation accrues too slowly to fake at scale. New identities start in a low-trust tier and can only wander into higher-value transactions after peers attest to consistent behavior. No ivory-tower audit replaces this: stake, slow history, and peer attestation together make spawning thousands of fake agents cost more than they can earn.
